messages:
olivia-eng: FYI — attempted restore of tenant-42 DB snapshot from glacier tier in staging failed with decryption error. Not sure if its KMS vs SSE-C mismatch, need help triage

sam-sre: paste the error logs and the s3 path you used pls

olivia-eng: logs:
```
2026-03-18T14:03:12Z restore: Start
2026-03-18T14:03:14Z s3:GetObject failed: AccessDenied. server side encryption mismatch
2026-03-18T14:03:14Z kms:Decrypt failed for arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01-2345
Error: AccessDeniedException: Caller is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on the key
```
Uploaded with backup-agent -> s3 multipart. Headers included: x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256 and x-amz-server-side-encryption-customer-key-sha256 present (so looks like SSE-C).

ben-infra: that header is SSE-C. Our cloud pipeline uses SSE-KMS by default; a few tenants/on-prem agents still used SSE-C historically. Restore path assumes SSE-KMS and calls KMS.Decrypt — which explains the ACL error.

sara.security: two immediate fronts: (1) RBAC for kms:Decrypt on the restore role and least-privileges, (2) auditability for the decryption/restore flow. Note SSE-C uploads bypass KMS (so no CloudTrail kms:Decrypt events) — we must ensure we record key fingerprints and operator identity in our backup metadata and enable vault audit.

sam-sre: short-term mitigation proposal: add SSE-C branch in restore service: if object contains SSE-C headers, read the key-sha256 from metadata, attempt vault lookup (Hashi transit/secret path) under the restore-role, pull the key material, decrypt locally and proceed. That requires vault read RBAC and explicit audit events for vault reads.

ben-infra: agreed. For the KMS path we should not give broad kms:Decrypt. Create scoped IAM role with narrow policy like:
```
{
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
  "Resource": ["arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01-2345"],
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"kms:ViaService": "s3.amazonaws.com"}}
}
```
For SSE-C restores we'll rely on vault access instead.

sara.security: also enable CloudTrail data events for s3:GetObject and CloudTrail for kms:Decrypt. Create an alert that flags restore operations that hit AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt so we auto-open an incident ticket. Ensure restore audit record includes: requestor, tenant id, object path, and key fingerprint (only hashed). Never persist raw key bytes.

olivia-eng: tenant-42 note: legacy snapshot, uploaded by their infra team last year with SSE-C. They granted ephemeral upload access but the key is in their vault, not ours — so restore failed. Ill update the incident ticket and reach out to tenant infra.

sam-sre: volunteer actions:
- add SSE-C branch to restore path to attempt vault lookup (sam-sre)
- create restore-s3-sse-kms scoped IAM role (ben-infra)
- add CloudTrail rules + alert on kms AccessDenied during restore (sara.security)
- update runbook to document SSE-C tenant verification and key escrow steps (olivia-eng)

oncall-bot: scheduled: runbook-test job queued for 2026-03-19T09:00Z (ID: rb-20260319-07)

kms-bot: policy-sim result: proposed restore role policy allows Decrypt on tenant keys for current tests; no broad wildcard detected.

sara.security: long-term: deprecate SSE-C for backups in shared S3 unless tenant keys are escrowed into our vault under contract. For on-prem/air-gapped backups define a clear escrow pattern: tenant provides wrapping key to customer-managed HSM/KMS and we get an access-controlled unwrap-only token. Also enforce separation of duties: ops may trigger restore but must not be able to extract raw tenant keys.

ben-infra: terraform snippet for role (WIP) — will open PR for review:
```
resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "restore_kms_policy" {
  role = aws_iam_role.restore_role.id
  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17",
    Statement = [
      { Effect = "Allow", Action = ["kms:Decrypt"], Resource = ["${var.tenant_key_arn}"] }
    ]
  })
}
```

olivia-eng: ack. Ill update ticket, plan to have SSE-C branch and runbook update by 2026-03-22. Will post results after staging validation.

sara.security: final reminders: every vault read must emit an audit event with requestor, tenant id, key fingerprint. No raw key storage in backups metadata. Include the terraform policy changes in PRs and tag sec for review.

sam-sre: will open PRs tomorrow and tag @sara.security. Closing loop soon :thumbsup:
